risk.rationale: Alpine conditions plus unresolved car, ferry, and flight gates create material exposure (2/5), while the canonical Valbona plan remains the family out-and-back rather than an incompatible full crossing.

budget.rationale: The six categories reconcile exactly to $10,700–$14,800. The floor sits below the $12k target and the whole band stays under the $15k preferred maximum — genuinely good value, and cheaper than nearly every peer whose budget scores 1. It falls short of a 4 only because the high case ($14,800) exceeds the $13,500 mid-band ceiling, driven by the two-stop LJU airfare. Cost is a reason to pick this trip.

weather.rationale: A genuine split: the Piran coast is warm and mostly dry in June (~25–28°C), but the Julian Alps see frequent June afternoon thunderstorms and the Vršič Pass carries a real late-snow timing risk. swim.rationale: The Piran Adriatic is a swimmable ~22°C / 72°F in June — warmer and calmer than the Atlantic plans but cooler than the Greek/Crete lagoons, off rocky platforms rather than warm sand. The glacial Soča and Alpine lakes are look-and-raft, not swim. Usable, limited, and refreshing water scores 3; Croatia, the obvious warm partner, is excluded by family decision.

variety.rationale: Alpine lakes, an emerald river, three gorges, a UNESCO cave, a mountain pass, a Venetian coast, and a capital city across one compact country is the full spread of water, towns, and nature.

ease.rationale: On the ground this is one of the easiest plans on the board: one country, one rental car, four bases in a tidy loop, short drives, no intra-Europe flight and no open-jaw. It scores 3 rather than higher only because Ljubljana has no long-haul service, so the air routing is a two-stop itinerary with a fragile final leg.

food.rationale: Every base (Bled, Bohinj, Bovec, Piran, Ljubljana) has full supermarkets (Mercator/Spar) plus reliable wood-fired pizza, pasta, and burgers — strong picky-eater coverage. It is inexpensive, but cost is scored under budget, not food.

risk.rationale: Lower risk than a multi-country Alpine plan: a single country, one rental car, no open-jaw or intra-Europe flight. weather.rationale: A genuine split: Sicily's Ionian and southeast coasts are hot and dry in June (~80–84°F highs), but the Berner Oberland sees rain on well over half of June days and Jungfraujoch can white out. The blended score reflects the real risk on the two marquee summit days.

swim.rationale: The seven Sicily nights deliver a strong ~72–75°F Ionian with the sheltered Isola Bella cove and the warm sandy shallows of Fontane Bianche — the same warm-water week that scores 4 on the Sicily-peer trips.
